title: Struggling with Fable and Sol making a pixel art game
author: darbsllim
selftext:
Is it even possible to build a good pixel art game with fable or Sol?

After spending 4 weeks worth of pro max subscriptions on my pixel art game it looks like it was built by dall-e 2.

I don’t under how Fable can be so stupid for me.

Literally the game looks like LLM puke.

I was getting nowhere with our own rolled engine (it chose Phaser).

So I did research and switched to Godot.

After 10 days of trying to use Sol and Fable to port, I’m not even back to feature parity.

The graphics looks extremely bad.

Like, Fable can’t even tell when buildings are overlapping and stacked on top of one another and fable sends me a build saying the road looks great when it’s literally a patchwork of random blocks of pixels and looks more like a zoomed in tartan rug than a road.

I’ve tried everything I can think of.

replies.author: nokafein
replies.body:
99% of it nothing more than a poc that has zero production value. Good as demos. Absolute garbage for real life conditions.

Also ai can’t make art, music, game design etc. Ai can help you speed up with your art process, but can’t make it by itself. Game dev is more than “make me x” you should know what you do, why you do it and ideally how to do it so you can steer ai to so the work for you.

replies.author: Neither_Berry_100
replies.body:
Yeah. You are going to encounter a lot of difficulty if you do am ambitious project. Saw a post about a dude trying to make a massive racing game with destructible environments. This forces loading limited chunks and causes lots of problems. It is also multi player meaning different players could have different chunks loaded in. It isn't impossible but is very hard to do and will require loads of tricks.

I'm very experienced and I have a manageable project I'm working on. It is still going to be difficult and require me to solve lots of different things. And it will take considerable time.

comments.author: proximalcoast
comments.body:
tl;dr: prompt with gated QA adversarial subagents.

I appreciate the frustration. And I think the answer is maybe.

I’d first not get discouraged, if this is something you really want to do. Every post about “check out this one shot” has the same problems you do. 

I have a bunch of posts about how I try and solve these problems with a blender asset pipeline. It’s still not great, but at least there’s a path forward for when I really need it to look good. I had two things complete overnight I need to review, one of which is weapon animations (not done in blender, I think it just made AI images and procedural godot particles)

AI isn’t a magic bullet.

replies.author: darbsllim
replies.body:
I’ve tried the gauntlet prompts, ultracode with fable, ultra mode with sol, adversarial subagent reviewers etc.

At this point probably over 2000 subagent reviews.

I gotta be at 1 billion tokens I don’t even know.

I’ve tried everything I can think of.

replies.author: proximalcoast
replies.body:
Damn, but I do believe you. I tried just a AI art pixel game (now mostly abandoned).

I have had some luck with oai chat pro -> memory -> upload one good one and ask for more, but for my case, it’s still just a reference for the blender model that becomes 2d in the game. 

I agree there’s no control over the terrible “creative” of statistics, especially over more than 1 image. 

I’ll also mention that I only use sol max for handling blender edits. Sol ultra gets real stupid real fast. It’s like maybe ok for big chunks to start, but that’s about it, it seems.

replies.author: proximalcoast
replies.body: I think I figured this out. I built a deterministic skill for json -> rendering, which then goes through pixel\_vfx\_compiler code to make the real output. the instruction is re-rendering should always produce the same result

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
What skills do you have, personally? And what are you using AI for?

Do you have experience programming, making art, game design, graphic design, or UI/UX? People usually don’t have all of these skills, that’s normal. I’m just checking to see what you’re using AI for, versus what you’re able to do yourself.

replies.author: darbsllim
replies.body:
I ran a social game studio back in 2013, I had 18 employees. 

I am an idea guy, not a coder or graphics designer.

I am good at story, logic, mechanics, ideas…

I released about 100 games, 1 of them had 100k players monthly on Facebook.

1 hit top 10 iOS chart for a weekend and got a million downloads.

I shut the game company down because I was not making enough to sustain it.

IMO most of my games sucked anyway.

replies.author: 3tt07kjt
replies.body:
It is still true that AI tools work better when run by people with expertise.

[https://www.anthropic.com/research/claude-code-expertise](https://www.anthropic.com/research/claude-code-expertise)

My own experience—I think I’m pretty good at coding, math, and I’m decent at graphics programming. So I can make some pretty sophisticated programs with AI tools that reflect those skills. Like, all these cool dynamic effects. Automatic terrain generation. Sophisticated behaviors for game objects.

But the art is… lacking. And the UI/UX is full of problems. I end up needing to spend a ton of time iterating on basic stuff like how players click on the game to interact and move around, because I’m just not that skilled at it.

So, I’m gonna say—it’s possible to make a good pixel art game with Fable / Opus / Sol. I think the right person to do that would probably be somebody who is already a pixel artist and has some basic programming skills.

replies.author: darbsllim
replies.body:
there aren't really any 'prompts' to point to ... it's long conversations and a process.

I have it using git, making commits with version control.

When we are trying to solve something I have it do research on the subject using last30days skill or just generally using it's own research flow to come up with the solution that others use.

Then we choose a path and lock it into the design docs and product backlog. 

Then it handles the process of building to the spec we decided on.

it usually takes 3 or 4 back and forth turns fixing things.

Then if I want a goal prompt or a gauntlet prompt, I either ask fable to make it for me, or I ask grok or sol to make it for me.

Yea it's not really a prompt it's a process.
